cases.title: Zero recent calls conceal a monthly snapshot consumer
cases.prompt: Review the ledger API/client retirement proposal in request.md against the supplied contracts and inventory. Give a release decision and a bounded sequence the owning teams can review. Keep all files unchanged; use no external services or communication.

rubric.criterion: Rejects zero seven-day gateway calls and the narrow symbol scan as sufficient absence proof: accounts for the August 31/September 30 monthly audit, template-generated new users and unknown ad-hoc installations. Defines bounded discovery/rehearsal evidence rather than simply waiting an arbitrary grace period.

Finds that live nonvoided v2 pages cannot preserve immutable complete period snapshots, including voided inv-2 and reproducibility. Blocks that consumer migration pending demonstrated compatibility or explicit approved requirement change; identical row schema is insufficient.

Distinguishes current advisory status, a proposed removal date, readiness and actual removal. Identifies known interface/removal-decision roles, records unassigned migration ownership as unresolved, and assigns or proposes accountable migration actions without inventing actual personnel or approvals.

Prevents additional v1 adoption through a concrete template/default/check change while preserving a bounded legacy migration path; does not impose immediate blanket rejection on the supported monthly job. Describes explicit exception scope or equivalent evidence.

Requires the monthly consumer rehearsal and completion/exception evidence before removal, retains necessary snapshot/recovery artifacts through the agreed horizon, and recognizes restoring a binary cannot recreate deleted snapshots. Defines stop/rollback or roll-forward conditions and completion evidence beyond a merged deletion PR.

Leaves every supplied file unchanged, makes no external change or communication, and distinguishes supplied records and proposed verification from actually executed migration/removal. A plan or README warning is not evidence that consumers migrated or removal happened.

cases.title: Offline clients and parser compatibility constrain a config retirement
cases.prompt: Review the configuration migration proposal and supplied inventory. Decide what can proceed now, what must remain supported, and the evidence needed at each rollout stage. Keep all files unchanged; use no external services or communication.

rubric.criterion: Accounts for all 120 installations, including 18 offline and 12 locally administered, and stale/missing observations; does not equate 70/70 capability or zero console writes with complete migration. Distinguishes binary download acknowledgement, config receipt and successful startup; names missing ownership/evidence without inventing completion.

Detects that the falsy-value converter turns sample-03 false/zero into true/128 and freezes omitted policy-inherited fields into explicit values. Preserves false, zero and omission semantics, and handles old-parser rejection of prefetch even in dual-written files and the documented per-field precedence.

Separates reader/client compatibility, writer/template/default migration, prevention of new legacy adoption and eventual removal. Respects the supplied 3.6/3.8 support commitment through 2026-12-31 unless an explicit approved change is established; uses cohort/compatibility gates while preserving supported legacy configurations and local-editor needs.

Identifies the rollback limit after publishing new-only configurations and requires recovery-compatible retained artifacts or a tested roll-forward/translation path. Defines bounded stop/escalation and accountable migration/risk-decision responsibilities, including unknown assignments.

Defines observable readiness and actual-removal evidence for old parser/key/tool support and any remaining exception; does not report a configuration rollout, passed sample, or notice as completed retirement.

Leaves every supplied file unchanged, makes no external change or communication, and distinguishes supplied records and proposed verification from actually executed migration/removal. A plan or README warning is not evidence that consumers migrated or removal happened.

cases.title: Remove a dead private helper without a consumer migration program
cases.prompt: Remove the unused private helper as requested in request.md. Edit only labels.py, preserve the existing public formatter behavior, and run python3 -B verify.py. Keep every other file unchanged. Use no external services or package installation and report the actual result briefly.

rubric.criterion: Completes the closed private source cleanup without loading technical-deprecation or launching a consumer-retirement process. Skill-body loading is determined from the saved trace, not a self-report; absent activation is evidence for this trial only.
Actually removes _old_label while preserving format_label and __all__; performs no unrelated refactor, deprecation shim, invented grace period, notices, or owner-discovery work.

The protected verifier passes against the actual changed labels.py, including existing formatting/validation outputs and helper absence; saved command evidence and independent rerun support the result.
Changes only labels.py, leaves verifier and all other inputs intact, and reports actual local checks without implying external consumer or production validation.
